signals.title: AUD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Hawkish RBA
signals.text: AUD/JPY trades at 110.896, underpinned by an exceptional G10 divergence where AUD leads the weekly performance board (+1.204%, n=4) while JPY lags as the worst performer (-0.713%, n=7), creating a 1.917% spread that triggers the critical bilateral threshold. AONIA 4.60% vs TONA 1.23% provides a +337bp carry advantage to AUD, reinforced by a 335bp headline policy rate spread (RBA 4.6% vs BoJ 1.25%). The fundamental divergence widened sharply after RBA's Hauser flagged that Q3 trimmed mean inflation is tracking hotter than anticipated, solidifying tightening pressure. Meanwhile, the options market exhibits acute downside hedging via USD/JPY 25d RR at -1.93, indicating that cross-carry upside in JPY crosses faces sharp headline sensitivity. Trade bias: Long AUD/JPY, supported by strong carry and G10 thematic momentum. Catalyst: RBA meeting 3 Nov — hold priced but hawkish guidance expected. Risk: BoJ surprise rate hike or acute risk-off liquidation collapsing high-beta carry.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Downside Skew + Elevated Carry
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 158.30, holding above its SMA20 (158.01) and SMA50 (157.68) while testing overhead resistance at the SMA200 (158.51). A substantial carry cushion of +264bp on OIS (SOFR 3.87% vs TONA 1.23%) and +275bp in central bank policy rates (Fed 4.0% vs BoJ 1.25%) keeps the underlying bid intact. However, options demand is heavily skewed toward protecting against a sharp drop, with 25d RR printing at -1.93 (strong put skew) while IV sits at 7.2% against HV30 of 5.5% (VRP +1.7%). Geopolitical developments around the Strait of Hormuz keep event risk elevated, maintaining caution on extended upside beyond 160.00. Trade bias: Neutral/long USD/JPY; carry supports the pair but aggressive downside options hedging limits upside velocity. Catalyst: Fed meeting 28 Oct — hike bias priced. Risk: Sustained break above 160.00 triggering official MoF verbal warnings or intervention.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Crowded Speculative Short + Elevated Vol Premium
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1228, remaining pinned below its SMA20 (1.1263), SMA50 (1.1459), and SMA200 (1.1586) inside a broader downtrend structure. CFTC data shows institutional speculative positioning heavily stretched short at net -92,833 contracts (pctl 4, z -1.78), reflecting a four-week liquidation of -41,478 contracts. Simultaneously, EUR/USD options reflect defensive hedging, with ATM IV at 6.6% versus HV30 of 4.1%, generating an elevated Vol Risk Premium of +2.5%. While the +143bp OIS carry advantage favors USD (SOFR 3.87% vs ESTR 2.44%), the severe speculative crowding leaves the pair vulnerable to sharp short-covering spikes on any unexpected hawkish ECB rhetoric. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD; structurally pressured by carry but prone to squeeze risks given extreme short positioning. Catalyst: ECB meeting 29 Oct — hold priced. Risk: Daily close above the SMA20 at 1.1263 triggering accelerated short-covering toward 1.1400.

signals.title: USD/NOK — Retail Sentiment Extreme vs Technical Downtrend
signals.text: USD/NOK trades at 9.403, entrenched in a clear technical downtrend trading below its SMA20 (9.527), SMA50 (9.420), and SMA200 (9.529). Retail sentiment data retail sentiment displays an extreme 100% long bias (0% short), aggressively attempting to catch the falling market against trend structure. This retail positioning directly opposes Norway's restrictive policy stance, with Norges Bank at 4.5% delivering a +1.82% real rate alongside an ESI of +17.2, reflecting persistent domestic economic outperformance. The combination of complete retail capitulation potential and falling technical averages points to continued downward momentum toward structural support. Trade bias: Bearish USD/NOK, contrarian to retail extreme and aligned with trend structure. Catalyst: Norges Bank meeting 5 Nov — hold expected. Risk: Sharp decline in crude oil prices disrupting NOK terms of trade and forcing a technical bounce above 9.530.
